deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a printed business form (a 'zur Nachricht' notice) from the St. Petersburg bookseller Carl Röttger, Kaiserlicher Hofbuchhändler, local firm H. Schmitzdorff. It is addressed to the Braunschweig bookseller G. C. E. Meyer sen. and dated 'den 10/6. 76', i.e. 10 June 1876. A Russian firm may have used the Julian date, which would be 22 June 1876 Gregorian; that is my inference, not stated on the form.

The handwritten text (brown ink) reads: 'Herrn G. C. E. Meyer sen. i. Braunschweig zur Nachricht, daß „Zolotareff, théorie des nombres entiers etc.“ nicht zu beschaffen, da das Werk hier gänzlich vergriffen ist. — Hochachtungsvoll.' In English: the work 'Zolotareff, théorie des nombres entiers etc.' cannot be supplied because it is completely out of print in St. Petersburg.

A second hand in violet ink, evidently Meyer's, adds a forwarding note to his customer: 'Ich werde versuchen, ob ein Exemplar antiquarisch aufzutreiben [ist]. Ergebenst G C E Meyer.' In English: 'I will try whether a copy can be found second-hand.'

The book requested is E. I. Zolotarev's 1874 St. Petersburg doctoral dissertation, 'Теория целых комплексных чисел с приложением к интегральному исчислению' (Theory of complex integers, with an application to the integral calculus). It is written in Russian, and the order evidently used a French rendering of the title. Zolotarev's French account of his approach to ideal theory ('Sur la théorie des nombres complexes', J. de Math. pures et appl. (3) 6) appeared only in 1880.

The page shows that in mid-1876 Dedekind tried, through his local Braunschweig bookseller, to obtain Zolotarev's thesis. This was the period when he was recasting his own ideal theory, in the French 'Sur la théorie des nombres entiers algébriques' (Bulletin des sciences mathématiques, 1876–77). The reply was that the work was out of print. The next folio appears to be a second notice from the same firm about the same title, so the search apparently continued.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematical content.
The French title 'théorie des nombres entiers [complexes]' is an informal rendering of a Russian title. No French book of that title existed in 1876, which may itself have hindered the order.

results.what: Documentary evidence that Dedekind (via bookseller G. C. E. Meyer, Braunschweig) sought Zolotarev's 1874 thesis on the theory of complex integers in June 1876, and that it was out of print in St. Petersburg.
results.modern_name: Bibliographic/correspondence record; context: Zolotarev's local (valuation-theoretic) approach to the arithmetic of algebraic integers as an alternative to Dedekind–Kronecker ideal theory.
results.usually_credited_to: Zolotarev (1874 thesis; 1880 French paper) for the theory itself.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bookseller's notice with no mathematics. It is a minor but genuine historical datum: Dedekind was already trying to obtain Zolotarev's Russian thesis in 1876. This is earlier than Zolotarev's French 1880 publication made the work accessible in the West. It may interest historians of ideal theory, but it is not a mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: The violet signature line is more likely 'Ergebenst G C E Meyer' than 'Hochachtend[?] G C E Meyer'.
'ein Exemplar antiquarisch aufzutreiben' is grammatically missing a final 'ist' in the original; the transcription is otherwise correct.
The author's name is written roughly 'Zolotareff' (the first vowel could be read 'a'). It refers to E. I. Zolotarev (Золотарёв).
